question: What is the main goal of public education in disaster prevention?

options.A: To ensure hospitals have enough beds during a crisis
options.B: To help communities build resilience and minimize harm
options.C: To take the place of professional emergency rescue teams
options.D: To completely clear out all natural hazards from a community

explanation: You've got this! Public education gives people practical tools to reduce risks and protect themselves before professional help arrives. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why are ordinary citizens considered the first line of defense during a sudden disaster?

options.A: They are solely responsible for building evacuation routes
options.B: They possess advanced medical training for crises
options.C: On-scene citizens control government relief funds
options.D: They are already on the scene before emergency workers arrive

explanation: Spot on! Immediate actions taken by people right where a disaster happens often make the biggest difference in keeping everyone safe. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h1)

question: As a community health nurse, what is a key duty when preparing for disasters?

options.A: Breaking down emergency guidelines into simple steps for residents
options.B: Managing the national budget for disaster relief
options.C: Building storm shelters and reinforced concrete walls
options.D: Declaring a formal state of emergency in the region

explanation: Great job! Nurses act as a bridge, turning complex disaster plans into clear, everyday steps that everyone can easily follow. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h2)

question: A community nurse advocating for marginalized groups during disaster planning is primarily trying to achieve what?

options.A: Speed up the building of commercial property in the area
options.B: Ensure vulnerable populations receive equal safety provisions
options.C: Reduce the total number of emergency personnel needed
options.D: Secure extra funding for hospital construction projects

explanation: Exactly! Advocacy ensures that groups who might struggle during an evacuation are fully cared for in safety plans. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which group is often most vulnerable during a disaster due to reliance on continuous care or medical equipment?
explanation: Correct! Older adults often have chronic health needs and rely heavily on steady electricity and support that can fail during a crisis. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h3)

question: A community nurse is planning a flood drill for a neighborhood with many toddlers. What is the most important factor to keep in mind?

options.A: They depend entirely on adults for safe movement and basic needs
options.B: They know how to operate community emergency radios
options.C: They can easily read printed evacuation maps on their own
options.D: They are capable of carrying emergency supply backpacks

explanation: Well reasoned! Infants and young children cannot move themselves to safety and need direct adult help during emergencies. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is a great way to reach people with low reading skills during a public safety campaign?

options.C: Relying solely on written email newsletters

explanation: You got it! Pictures and clear demonstrations help share safety messages effectively with everyone in the community. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h4)

question: Why is it best to use local languages and trusted community figures when teaching disaster safety?

options.A: It prevents the government from spending money on ads
options.B: It is a strict legal requirement for all hospital workers
options.C: It stops people from asking questions about safety plans
options.D: It builds trust and ensures the message is easily understood

explanation: Spot on! People are much more likely to listen and take action when advice comes from a familiar, respected voice speaking their native language. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h4)

question: Which items are absolute must-haves in a basic household emergency kit?

options.A: Portable safe water and non-perishable food

explanation: Correct! Clean water and food are your top survival essentials when regular utilities and shops shut down during a disaster. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why should families pick a specific meeting place outside their home when planning for emergencies?

options.A: To ensure everyone can reunite safely if separated during an evacuation
options.B: To provide a storage space for heavy rescue tools
options.C: To serve as a temporary community clinic
options.D: To give neighbors a place to park their vehicles

explanation: Brilliant! Having a pre-arranged meeting spot saves precious time and stops panic if family members get separated during a sudden crisis. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h5)

question: What is the main reason for holding community disaster drills?

options.A: To replace the need for written emergency preparedness guides
options.B: To help residents turn emergency knowledge into practical muscle memory
options.C: To punish people who fail to follow local sanitation laws
options.D: To test the physical strength of professional rescue workers

explanation: You're doing great! Drills give people practice so they can react quickly and calmly when a real emergency strikes. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h6)

question: Why is a quick review session important right after finishing a community disaster simulation?

options.A: To identify weaknesses in the plan and discuss areas for improvement
options.B: To officially close down the community health center for repairs
options.C: To fine community members who moved too slowly
options.D: To hand out formal employment contracts to volunteers

explanation: Spot on! Reviewing the drill helps organizers and participants spot problems and fix safety gaps before a real disaster happens. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h6)

question: Which method is commonly used to check what people learned immediately after a disaster workshop?

options.A: Giving participants simple tests before and after the session
options.B: Measuring the depth of water in nearby rivers
options.C: Counting the number of commercial stores in the area
options.D: Checking the personal income tax records of attendees

explanation: Correct! Comparing scores before and after a training session is a quick way to see how much new knowledge participants picked up. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h7)

question: A nurse evaluates a disaster program and notices residents still cannot point out their local evacuation route. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Remove all warning signs to encourage independent learning
options.B: Report the community residents to local law enforcement
options.C: Assume the community is fully prepared and stop teaching
options.D: Change up the teaching style and provide follow-up education

explanation: You nailed it! Finding a learning gap just means it's time to try a new teaching approach so the community feels confident and prepared. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h7)
